name: Can a detached ADU be built on a small lot in Glendale or Pasadena?

mainEntity.name: Can a detached ADU fit on a small residential lot in Glendale or Pasadena if the yard is tight?
mainEntity.text: Can a detached ADU fit on a small residential lot in Glendale or Pasadena if the yard is tight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Small lots can still work for detached ADUs, but the usable yard area matters more than the lot size alone. A site that looks large enough can become tight once setbacks, fire access, drainage, easements, existing trees, and utility clearances are mapped. In Glendale and Pasadena, homeowners should expect the design to be driven by the site plan rather than by a standard model. The right first step is a feasibility study that measures the buildable envelope before any architectural rendering is finalized. That analysis should show where the ADU can sit, how service lines will reach it, whether there is room for a patio or walkway, and whether parking or driveway access becomes an issue. On small properties, a compact footprint and simple roofline often make the difference between a workable project and one that is too constrained to build efficiently. A contractor experienced in tight urban lots can often identify solutions that a generic prefab-style design cannot.
acceptedAnswer.description: A detached ADU may still be possible on a small lot if setbacks, access, height, and lot coverage allow it. The key question is not just lot size, but whether the remaining buildable area can support a code-compliant structure, pathway, and utility connections.
